title: Git Bisect for Your Data
why_read: A clever practical technique using database branching to binary-search through time for data bugs is a genuinely useful and creative idea for engineers debugging data issues.
analysis: This article applies the 'git bisect' concept to data debugging, using instant database branching (via Neon's copy-on-write branches) to query the database state at arbitrary past moments without restoring full backups. It gives concrete performance numbers, showing a single branch-and-query probe takes about 1.7 seconds, making a 24-hour bisect at one-minute resolution feasible in about 20 seconds instead of scanning every minute. This is a practical, well-quantified technique that could genuinely change how engineers debug silent data corruption issues in production.
